# The Urlcade

> A self-hosted game-authoring API, delivered as a URL-encoded virtual
> console: build a cart as a plain JS object, encode it to bytes, and
> the resulting URL fragment *is* the game — decoded and run by a
> static, modular JS runtime shared by every cart. No server, no build
> step, no install, no account. Copy a link, the recipient gets the
> exact game. Designed to be self-serve for an AI agent: read
> AUTHORING.md, click "+ New Cart" at https://canyonturtle.github.io/games/,
> and edit the cart source right there — specific compile errors, a
> live Play link, all in one page, no human in the loop required.

## Build a cart

- [AUTHORING.md](https://canyonturtle.github.io/games/AUTHORING.md): How to build a cart — the object shape, every field's meaning, the opcode table, the hook lifecycle, the map generators. Start here.
- [kernel.js](https://canyonturtle.github.io/games/kernel.js): The actual `encodeCart`/`decodeCart`/opcode table/assembler/VM/compression/disassembler — one dependency-free file, the single source of truth for the cart format (loaded directly, not copied, by every other file below). Runs standalone under Node or any JS host: no browser, no network, no build step (`const K = require('./kernel.js')`).
- [fixtures.md](https://canyonturtle.github.io/games/fixtures.md): Known-good (cart description → exact bytes → exact fragment string) examples generated by kernel.js. Check your own implementation against these directly — nothing here requires running anything.

## Play it, debug it, compile it — all one page

- [https://canyonturtle.github.io/games/](https://canyonturtle.github.io/games/): The live runtime. The shelf lists five playable cartridges (Flappy Bird, a racer, a roguelike, a platformer, and a physics-based castle-crusher); any validly-encoded cart fragment is directly playable at `/#<fragment>`, not only those five — paste one into the shelf's box and it plays.
- **Debug**, reachable from any playing game: decodes and visualizes the current cart (palette, sprites, tiles, map, entities, every hook disassembled to a labeled listing and a flowchart) across several tabs, plus two that make this a real authoring loop, not just a viewer — **Source** (the cart as an editable plain-JS-object literal, recompiling automatically as you type) and **Compile** (a specific, line-numbered error naming the failing hook, or byte/fragment size info and a "Play this version" button once it's clean). A successful edit updates every other tab live.
- **+ New Cart**, on the shelf: opens Debug on a small working starter cart, landed on the Source tab — the fastest way to go from nothing to a compiling, playable cart with zero setup.
